note: Default for every country whose standard workweek is Monday-Friday in the source, or that the source does not list (see docs/03-methodology.md, 'Weekend labels')
Saudi Arabia: workweek Sunday-Thursday (Royal Decree M/51, Art. 98, cited in source). Verified for the 2019-2020 data period
Israel: workweek Sunday-Thursday; some people work a partial Friday. Verified for 2019-2020
Palestine: workweek Saturday-Thursday (Labour Law No. 7 of 2000, Art. 68, cited in source). Friday only. Verified for 2019-2020
Iran: workweek Saturday-Thursday (Thursday shorter). Friday only. Verified for 2019-2020
Nepal: workweek Sunday-Friday. Saturday only. Verified for 2019-2020
India: standard workweek Monday-Saturday in source. Sunday only. Many offices also close Saturday; we follow the source
Hong Kong: workweek Monday-Saturday in source ('many people work on Saturday either a half-day or full-day'). Sunday only
Mexico: workweek Monday-Saturday in source. Sunday only
Bolivia: not listed in the 2019 revision; current revision gives Monday-Saturday. Assumed unchanged since 2020
Honduras: not listed in the 2019 revision; current revision gives Monday-Saturday. Assumed unchanged since 2020
Colombia: source gives 'Monday-Friday / Monday-Saturday'. First listed form used
Pakistan: source gives Monday-Friday but notes many businesses open Saturday. Listed form used
Philippines: source gives Monday-Friday but notes most businesses open Saturday. Listed form used
UAE: workweek Sunday-Thursday since September 2006 (source). No UAE station in the Lecocq data; needed for the UAE weekend experiment

UAE: federal workweek Monday-Friday with a half-day Friday from 2022-01-01. NOTE: Sharjah local government and private schools work Monday-Thursday (Friday-Sunday weekend), which matters for station II.UOSS in Sharjah
